issues.failure_explanation: Lemma 4.9 controls $v^h$ and its derivatives only on $(-R,R)^d$, so $u:=F(t_{k_m+1},\cdot;v^{h_m}(t_{k_m+1},\cdot))$ is bounded and Lipschitz, uniformly in $m$, only on that cube. Lemma 4.10's hypothesis requires $u\in C^{0,1}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ with the global norm, and the conclusion $J_m\to0$ needs that norm uniformly in $m$. In the annulus between $\partial(-R,R)^d$ and the boundary of the interpolant's compact support no stated result bounds the derivatives of $v^h(t_k,\cdot)$, so the invoked hypothesis is unverified.

failure_location.quote: Further, Assumption \ref{assum:4.1} and Lemma \ref{lem:4.9} imply that $F(t,\cdot;v^h(t,\cdot))$ is bounded and Lipschitz continuous. This together with Lemma \ref{lem:4.10} guarantees $J_m\to 0$ as $m\to\infty$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Extend $u|_{(-R,R)^d}$ to a bounded Lipschitz function $\tilde u$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with the same uniform bound (McShane extension); since $I(u)$ depends only on values on $\Gamma\subset(-R,R)^d$ and $y_m\in(-R,R)^d$, $J_m=\tilde u(y_m)-I(\tilde u)(y_m)$, and Lemma 4.10 applies to $\tilde u$.
issues.overall_effect: The consistency step $J_m\to0$ (control of the nonlinearity's collocation-interpolation error) in the proof of Theorem 4.5 is unjustified as written.
issues.title: Lemma 4.10 invoked for the nonlinearity interpoland whose global C^{0,1} norm is not established
issues.why_classification: A standard one-line extension argument repairs the step; every claim, rate and advertised scope of the paper survives unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: let $\varphi$ be a $C^3$-function on $[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d$ such that $\overline{v}-\varphi$ has a global strict maximum at $(t,x)$ with $(\overline{v}-\varphi)(t,x)=0$

issues.failure_explanation: In the third inequality of the chain, Lemma 4.11 is applied to $\varphi(t_{k_m+1},\cdot)$, where $\varphi$ is the arbitrary test function touching $\overline v$. The lemma is stated only for functions whose $C^3$-norm on $\mathcal{O}$ is at most the fixed constant $C_1$ coming from Lemma 4.9; an arbitrary test function has a finite but generally larger $C^3$-norm, so the invocation is outside the lemma's hypotheses. The direction actually needed (sup-inf $\le \varphi(x)-\delta F(D\varphi,D^2\varphi)+\mathrm{error}$) does hold for arbitrary $C^3$ test functions with an error constant depending on the function, since the proof of that direction uses the $C_1$-bound only through constants, and $C(\varphi)\delta_m^{1+\beta}\to0$ because $\varphi$ is fixed; but this observation is nowhere in the source.

failure_location.quote: With the representation (\ref{eq:4.5}), we apply Lemma \ref{lem:4.11} for the family $\{v^{h_m}(t_{k_m+1},\cdot), \varphi(t_{k_m+1},\cdot)\}_{m\ge 1}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate Lemma 4.11 (or add a remark) asserting its `$\le$' direction for arbitrary $C^3$ functions with an error constant depending on the $C^3$-norm, which the given proof already establishes with constant tracking; note that for the fixed test function $C(\varphi)\delta_m^{1+\beta}\to0$.
issues.overall_effect: The inequality replacing the test function's sup-inf by $\varphi-\delta_m F(D\varphi,D^2\varphi)$ in the subsolution argument of Theorem 4.5 is not covered by the stated lemma.
issues.title: Lemma 4.11 applied to the arbitrary viscosity test function outside its C^3-norm hypothesis
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local strengthening of the lemma's statement, verifiable from its own proof; the subsolution conclusion and all other claims survive with no new construction.

issues.failure_explanation: (4.4) bounds $v^{h_m}(t_{k_m+1},\cdot)$ by $\varphi+c_m+(\Delta t)_m^{3/2}$ with the maximal time step $(\Delta t)_m$; the chain instead inserts $\delta_m^{3/2}$, where $\delta_m=t_{k_m+1}-t_{k_m}\le(\Delta t)_m$, which does not follow from (4.4). With the corrected $(\Delta t)_m^{3/2}$, the final $o(1)$ after division by $\delta_m$ requires $(\Delta t)_m^{3/2}=o(\delta_m)$; Assumption 4.3 only imposes $\Delta t\to0$, and on non-quasi-uniform grids the near-maximizing step can satisfy $\delta_m\ll(\Delta t)_m$, making $(\Delta t)_m^{3/2}/\delta_m$ diverge, so the $o(1)$ is unproven.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Select exact maximizers of $v^{h_m}-\varphi$ over the finite time grid times $\mathbb{R}^d$ (attainment after the standard modification of $\varphi$ outside a neighbourhood of $(t,x)$ so that $v^h-\varphi\to-\infty$ at infinity), so that the slack is $0$; the argument is then valid for arbitrary grids with $\Delta t\to0$. Alternatively, assume quasi-uniform time grids so $\delta_m\asymp(\Delta t)_m$.
issues.overall_effect: The passage to the viscosity subsolution inequality for $\overline v$ in the proof of Theorem 4.5 is not justified as written for general time grids.
issues.title: Near-maximality slack $(\Delta t)_m^{3/2}$ silently replaced by $\delta_m^{3/2}$ in the main chain
issues.why_classification: A contained reworking of the maximizer selection (or a mild standard grid condition) repairs the step with no loss of conclusion or advertised scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then, considering $p=p_0$ and $\gamma=\gamma_0$, we find that the right-hand side in the above inequality is greater than $\varphi(x)-C\delta^{1+\beta} -\delta F(p_0,\gamma_0)$ with $\beta=1/2-3\theta>0$

issues.failure_explanation: Mirroring the subsolution chain at a touch-from-below point requires the opposite ('$\ge$') direction of Lemma 4.11 for the test function: $\sup_{(p,\gamma)\in\mathcal{D}}\inf_w[\varphi(\cdot)-\ldots-\delta F(p,\gamma)]\ge\varphi(x)-\delta F(D\varphi,D^2\varphi)-o(\delta)$. The proof of that direction chooses $(p,\gamma)=(D\varphi(x),D^2\varphi(x))\in\mathcal{D}$ and therefore needs $|D\varphi(t,x)|,|D^2\varphi(t,x)|\le C_1$. The viscosity supersolution property must be tested against arbitrary smooth functions, and any admissible touch from below can be modified by subtracting $M|y-x|^2$, making $\|D^2\varphi(t,x)\|$ arbitrarily large while remaining a valid test; for such test functions the required estimate genuinely fails (the sup over the fixed $\mathcal{D}$ realizes $-\delta F(D\varphi,D^2\varphi)$ only up to $O(\delta)$, or worse through terms of order $\delta^{1-2\theta}$ from the Hessian quadratic). Hence the 'similar argument' does not exist within the paper's framework, and the supersolution half of the Barles-Souganidis program is unproven.

failure_location.quote: A similar argument shows that $$\underline{v}(t,x)=\liminf_{{t_k\to t,\; y\to x}\atop{h\searrow 0}}v^{h}(t_k,y), \quad (t,x)\in [0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d$$ is a viscosity supersolution of (\ref{eq:1.1}).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a contained argument: either (i) exploit the odd symmetry of the scheme - for $\tilde F(t,x,z,p,\gamma):=-F(t,x,-z,-p,-\gamma)$, which satisfies Assumption 4.1, and data $-f$, the collocation solution satisfies $\tilde v^h=-v^h$ (the interpolation is linear and the recursion commutes with negation), so applying the already-given subsolution argument to the transformed problem shows $-\underline v$ is a subsolution of the transformed equation, equivalent to $\underline v$ being a supersolution of (1.1); or (ii) argue directly at exact minima of the smooth differences $v^{h_m}(t_{k_m},\cdot)-\varphi(t_{k_m},\cdot)$ (where $Dv^{h_m}=D\varphi$ and $D^2v^{h_m}\succeq D^2\varphi$), using Lemma 4.9(ii), the degenerate parabolicity and Lipschitz continuity of $F$.
issues.overall_effect: Only the subsolution property of $\overline v$ is proved. The supersolution property of $\underline v$, hence $\overline v=\underline v=v$ and the convergence asserted in Theorem 4.5, is unsupported as written.
issues.title: Supersolution half of Theorem 4.5 asserted by 'a similar argument' that the paper's tools cannot carry out
issues.why_classification: The main theorem is unproven as written, but a correct proof is available inside the paper's own framework through a contained additional argument (either option above), with no loss of scope, regime or rates and no new global proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Next, take $\delta_1\in (0,1]$ such that $x+\sqrt{\delta}w\in\mathcal{O}$ for all $w\in\mathcal{X}_{\delta,\theta}$, and $\delta\le\delta_1$.

issues.failure_explanation: $\varphi$ is defined only on $\mathcal{O}$, while the displayed sup-inf evaluates $\varphi(x+\sqrt{\delta}w)$ for all $|w|\le\delta^{-\theta}$, i.e. at points up to distance $\delta^{1/2-\theta}$ from $x$. For $x\in\mathcal{O}$ with $\mathrm{dist}(x,\partial\mathcal{O})<\delta^{1/2-\theta}$ the left-hand side is undefined, so no single $\delta_1>0$ makes the stated quantification over all $x\in\mathcal{O}$ meaningful; the proof itself first fixes $(t,x,z)$ and then chooses $\delta_1$ depending on that $x$, so it establishes only a pointwise-in-$x$ version, materially weaker than the statement.
